source:
Backyard Monsters is one of the most underappreciated strategy games ever made. It combined Clash of Clans, Factorio, tower defense, RTS, and idle progression years before most mobile games. The core loop was: build a monster base, gather resources, research new monsters, attack other players, and defend your own base while upgrades continued in real time.
I actually think a Roblox spiritual successor could be bigger than the original, because Roblox solves many of the social and multiplayer limitations that Facebook games had.

The Fantasy
You're not building a town.
You're growing a monster civilization hidden inside a suburban backyard.
Imagine:
 • gigantic mushrooms
 • monster nests
 • slime rivers
 • tree forts
 • toy blocks
 • abandoned bicycles
 • sprinklers become rivers
 • garden hoses become bridges
 • sandbox becomes a desert biome
The world feels gigantic because you're tiny.

Core Gameplay Loop

Login

↓

Collect resources

↓

Upgrade buildings

↓

Breed new monsters

↓

Scout nearby players

↓

Attack enemy bases

↓

Steal resources

↓

Expand territory

↓

Unlock stronger monsters

↓

Repeat

Every mechanic feeds this loop.

Battle Gameplay
Here's where I'd improve massively.
Old Backyard Monsters was mostly click-and-watch.
Instead...
Hybrid RTS.

Base Defense
Every base should feel unique.
Defenses include
Spike traps
Acid pools

Terrain Matters

Tank

Makes every monster feel alive.

Exploration

Alliances

Members

Share resources.
Raid bosses.
Alliance wars.
Alliance tech tree.
Alliance fortress.

PvP

Raid

Ranked

Alliance vs Alliance.

Reputation
Instead of trophies only.
Neighborhood Reputation.
Higher reputation unlocks
NPC traders.
Legendary bosses.
Special cosmetics.
Elite players.

Endgame
Not just bigger numbers.
Players chase
Monster encyclopedia completion
Perfect mutations
Rare decorations
Alliance rankings
Seasonal leaderboards
World bosses
Legendary base skins

Live Events
Weekly
Meteor crashes.
Alien invasion.
Backyard flooded.
Neighborhood barbecue.
Halloween monsters.
Christmas toy factory.
Every event changes gameplay.

Idle Progression
Offline
Resources continue.
Research continues.
Breeding continues.
Monster healing continues.
Expeditions continue.
Enough idle to respect players' time, but not so much that active play feels unnecessary.

Roblox-Specific Improvements
This is where a clone can become something much larger.
Instead of every player living in an isolated instance, imagine an entire persistent neighborhood server with 20-40 players.
Each player owns one backyard, but everyone can:
 • Walk to neighboring yards.
 • Watch live attacks.
 • Trade monster DNA.
 • Visit alliance fortresses.
 • Participate in neighborhood events (like defending against a giant cat invading multiple bases).
This makes the world feel alive in a way the original never could.

Technical Architecture

Server
├── Persistent World
├── Base Simulation
├── Resource Production
├── Combat Engine
├── Pathfinding
├── AI Behavior Trees
├── Research System
├── Alliance System
├── Matchmaking
├── Economy
└── Live Events

Client
├── Building Mode
├── RTS Controls
├── Combat VFX
├── Monster Animation
├── UI
├── Camera
└── Audio

Each player's base is an independently simulated "island" within the larger neighborhood, allowing efficient server performance while still supporting social interactions and live events.

Long-Term Retention
The best strategy games always have goals on multiple timescales:
 • 5-minute session: Collect resources, queue upgrades, check breeding results, attack one nearby base.
 • 30-minute session: Explore a new biome, defeat a boss, redesign your defenses, experiment with a new army composition.
 • Weekly goal: Complete alliance events, unlock a new monster family, climb ranked PvP, finish research branches.
 • Monthly goal: Earn limited seasonal monsters, evolve Ancient monsters, upgrade your fortress, and compete for neighborhood dominance.
The original Backyard Monsters proved that combining base building, asynchronous PvP, and long-term progression was compelling. A modern Roblox version could push that much further by emphasizing collectible monsters with unique AI, exploration beyond the home base, cooperative neighborhood gameplay, and a living world that changes through seasonal events rather than simply recreating the original formula.

answers.ask: Should we build one backyard base first, or the whole neighbourhood world map? Eight expanding world tiers will not fit in a single top-down image, so they would be separate maps.
answers.answer: Build one backyard base first as the playable vertical slice. The wider world map and its expanding tiers can come later as separate maps.

answers.ask: Are the neighbouring players' yards inside the same map as yours, or separate instances you travel to?
answers.answer: Neighbouring players' yards should be separate instances you travel to for scouting and raids, keeping each base focused and readable.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D top-down strategy map for one playable monster civilization base hidden in a suburban backyard, viewed at tiny-creature scale. Center the layout on a Monster Heart, with clear buildable territory branching outward for monster nests and housing, resource extractors and storages, laboratories, breeding caves, spell towers, defensive walls, turrets, traps, acid pools, slime launchers, poison flowers, Venus flytraps, and a future fortress footprint. Surround the base with oversized backyard terrain and landmarks: gigantic mushrooms, tall grass, trees and tree forts, slime rivers, a sprinkler-fed water channel, garden-hose bridges, toy blocks, abandoned bicycles, broken toys, soda cans, old tools, and a sandbox forming a small desert biome. Use height changes, mud, water, cover-providing trees and grass, and open approach routes to shape the terrain. Keep this yard as a focused standalone base map; neighboring player yards are separate destinations rather than visible plots in the same scene.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy, with RTS-style base building and territorial defense derived from the author’s progression and combat loop. Simulation is not needed as a secondary genre: its economy is contextual, while the playable space is organized around strategic placement, approaches, and defense.

### Shape and preset
Use `terrain-open`, matched from the Real-Time Strategy preset. This is one defended monster homeland rather than a lane-based tower-defense track: the Monster Heart anchors freely arranged structures and broad approach ground. Retain the preset’s open-territory logic, adapted to a tiny-creature backyard base.

### Config requirements
Use visible `buildzone-plot` for clear, branching buildable ground surrounding the Heart, with reserved pads for nests, housing, extractors, storages, labs, breeding caves, spell towers, defenses, and a future fortress. Use `tracker-core` as the visible central Monster Heart and its invisible core-status region. Use invisible `collectible-nodes` to place resource extraction points among thematic scrap, organic growth, and backyard debris. Use visible `cover-los` for trees, tall grass, mushrooms, toy clutter, and bicycle parts that break sightlines. Use visible `water-body` for slime rivers and the sprinkler-fed channel, crossed by hose bridges. Use visible `terrain-relief` for mud hollows, raised roots, sandbox dunes, and small height changes.

### Layout components
Place the Monster Heart at the center of a roughly circular, medium-sized defended clearing. Arrange dense inner build territory in radial branches around it: housing and nests closest to the Heart, storage and laboratories in protected mid-ground, and breeding caves, spell towers, turrets, traps, acid pools, slime launchers, poison flowers, and Venus flytraps nearer the defensive perimeter. Reserve a large rear or side footprint for the future fortress. Defensive walls form irregular partial rings with several readable open approach routes rather than a sealed symmetrical enclosure.

A slime river crosses one outer side, while a sprinkler-fed water channel cuts through another edge; garden hoses form narrow bridges over both. The sandbox occupies one corner as a dry desert biome. Gigantic mushrooms, tall grass, trees, tree forts, toy blocks, abandoned bicycles, broken toys, soda cans, and old tools form oversized perimeter landmarks and cover clusters. Keep neighboring yards absent: this is one standalone backyard map with implied off-map travel destinations. Frame it as a high three-quarter strategic overview, Heart centered and the backyard landmarks establishing the tiny scale.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: the authoritative first image is a top-down plan so buildable territory, wall gaps, water crossings, and attack approaches remain legible and connected; dress the isometric view from that plan.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, driven by one complete playable base and its surrounding backyard landmarks rather than the later world tiers. Theme: whimsical dark-fantasy monster civilization in a colossal suburban backyard. Use `tiered` for non-overhanging terrain relief and `CHECK` because the rivers and channels are real water features; no separate-map or interior pass is required.
